claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of as-cast, homogeneous FeNiCrMn is governed by a transition between deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
Low temperatures combined with high strain rates limit dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Limited dislocation mobility promotes early nucleation of deformation twins in FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twins impede dislocation motion and thereby enhance strain hardening while preserving the strength–ductility balance.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, dislocation glide and recovery dominate in FeNiCrMn.
Higher temperatures or lower strain rates produce lower twin density and a softer response in FeNiCrMn.
The target as-cast FeNiCrMn is a homogeneous solid solution with an equiaxed grain structure and minimal secondary phases or defect segregation.
Twin density and distribution relative to dislocation structures are the structural mediator connecting temperature and strain rate to mechanical response.
Reduced thermal activation at low temperature restricts dislocation mobility.
Increased dislocation mobility at higher temperature or lower strain rate causes predominant slip, dynamic recovery, and minimal twin formation.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate testing will produce higher dynamic yield strength in FeNiCrMn.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate testing will produce more pronounced strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
The increased yield strength and strain hardening at low temperature and high strain rate will correlate with increased deformation-twin density.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, FeNiCrMn will exhibit predominant dislocation slip, lower twin density, and reduced strain hardening.
At room temperature and moderate strain rate, FeNiCrMn plasticity is dominated by dislocations with minimal twinning.
Significant segregation, secondary phases, or introduced defects may alter the proposed deformation mechanisms.
